t: Sukarno led the nationalist movement against Dutch rule, spent over a decade in Dutch detention, and with Mohammad Hatta declared Indonesian independence on 17 August 1945, after which he led the resistance to Dutch re-colonisation until recognition in 1949.

In 1959 he replaced a quarrelling parliamentary system with the authoritarian Guided Democracy, and in the early 1960s he pursued an aggressive foreign policy while the economy deteriorated and the Communist Party grew under his protection.

After the 30 September Movement of 1965, General Suharto took control, between 500,000 and over 1 million people were killed in the purge that followed, and Sukarno spent his last years under house arrest.
dyk: In his speech of 1 June 1945 Sukarno set out five principles, known as pancasila, that he saw as shared by all Indonesians; the version put into effect in the 1945 Constitution omitted the reference to Islamic law that an earlier draft had carried.
ev: Sukarno is born in Surabaya, in the Dutch East Indies
He and friends from a Bandung study club found the Indonesian National Party, and he becomes its first leader
At his trial in Bandung he delivers the speeches published as Indonesia Accuses and is sentenced to four years in prison
The Dutch governor-general sends him without trial into internal exile, first on Flores and from 1938 at Bengkulu
Sukarno and Hatta proclaim Indonesian independence on 17 August, and the next day Sukarno is elected president
He hosts the Bandung Conference of Asian and African countries
He restores the 1945 constitution by decree and begins Guided Democracy
Under the order known as Supersemar he transfers most presidential authority to Suharto, and he is placed under house arrest the next year

f.born: 6 June 1901 in Surabaya, East Java, Dutch East Indies, originally named Kusno Sosrodihardjo; son of Raden Soekemi Sosrodihardjo, a Javanese primary school teacher and priyayi, and Ida Ayu Nyoman Rai, a Balinese Hindu of the Brahmin caste
f.died: 21 June 1970 in Jakarta Army Hospital of kidney failure, while under house arrest; buried in Blitar, East Java, next to his mother
f.role: Leader of the Indonesian National Party (from 1927); head of the Investigating Committee for Preparatory Work for Independence (1945); first president of Indonesia, 1945 to 1967, elected president for life by the MPRS in 1963 and stripped of the title in 1967
f.known: the Indonesian independence movement; the Proclamation of 17 August 1945; Pancasila; Guided Democracy; the Bandung Conference and the Non-Aligned Movement; the campaigns over West Irian and against Malaysia; his fall after the events of 1965
